title: Scope key type, defaults, caps and K0 with a derived primitive
summary: @inventarch/runtime exports the scope key K = (seat, shape, phase, depth, budget, word) as the ScopeKey type, its caps as SCOPE_KEY_CAPS ({depth: 2, budget: 64}) and K0, the frozen key with no seat, shape context, phase orient, depth 0, budget 0 and no word. normalizeScopeKey(partial) completes a partial key with the defaults of the position design: a partial that names no part (a part whose value is undefined is not named) returns K0; otherwise shape defaults to context, phase to the anchor phase of the shape's primitive (context orient, governance plan, execution act, sequence plan, learning learn), depth to 1 and budget to 16, and the seat and the word stay absent unless named. It reads nothing, so it checks the key's form and leaves the word and the seat to resolveScopeKey. resolveScopeKey(handle, within, key) checks a complete key against a scoped read and returns a frozen {key, seat, resolution, coordinate}: the shape must be one of the five shapes, the phase one of the four phases, depth an integer in 0..2, budget an integer in 0..64 and the word, when given, one the read's view registers; any other part, a primitive included, is refused. Every key refusal of either function is IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID naming the closed set or bound, and the parts, closed sets, caps and seat form are checked before any read, so a key malformed in them is refused whatever the token; a forged, stale or closed token keeps its database code (IA-DB-SCOPE-UNAVAILABLE, IA-DB-STALE or IA-DB-CLOSED). The resolved seat is a ResolvedSeat {kind, identity, path, unknown}: kind workspace when the key names no seat, its identity the `@workspace` the database seats the repository root at; record when the key names an identity, which must be an admitted record in the scope; location when the key names {path}, its path the canonical workspace-relative path, with no identity. A path may be workspace-relative or absolute inside the handle's root; an absolute one reads as the path from the root that Node's path.relative gives (on Windows without case and with either separator), and the root itself, however it is spelled, as the location '' that . also names. A path outside the root, one that escapes it through a .. segment and an absolute path on another drive are refused, while an in-root name that only begins with .., such as ..cache, is accepted in either spelling. The returned key carries a location as that canonical relative path, never the root. For a workspace or location seat, resolution is the database's resolveSeat result: the record declared there, the rule that declares it and the path's claimants. A seat inside the workspace that no record in the scope is declared at is not refused: the seat names unknown undeclared (a workspace seat then has no identity), so K0 stays computable when the repository's own `@workspace` is undecided. The coordinate declares the key's shape and phase and derives category and primitive from the shape's SHAPE_ROWS row, so a key with only a shape and a phase is complete. The new @inventarch/runtime/internal/scope-key subpath carries the module, and @inventarch/runtime/internal/coordinate adds scopeCoordinate. The @inventarch/db readers (Handle, ReadHandle and the editor reader) add words(options): the frozen, sorted words the read view's registry registers for its admitted systems, the floor's two included. Options bind as get binds them, every scope of a view reads the same words, the capture pair is never read and the registry stays private. Limits: positionBody assembles the body a resolved key gives, and no host note is assembled; no Door operation or CLI command takes a key, and prepareCoordinate, context, select, the nine version 1 Door routes and ia scope are unchanged, so a context or select request without a declared primitive is still refused as coordinate-incomplete.
